title: Support Conduit: compile runbooks into telemetry-driven executable tasklets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build 'Support Conduit' — a compiler and runtime that turns canonical runbooks into small, versioned 'tasklets' that can be executed by the admin-runner with telemetry-driven fallbacks and automatic audit logging. The tasklet format should be pluggable (shell steps, API calls, parameterized queries) and enforce idempotency, RBAC checks, and simulated dry-run prior to production execution.

Why: Current runbooks are long markdown documents; oncall and first-line support need fast, safe, repeatable remediations. Conduit will reduce mean time to remediation (MTTR) for common classes of incidents and make automation discoverable and auditable.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include a full UI for composing tasklets (follow-up). It also will not implement multi-tenant scheduling or cross-account execution (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook canonical YAML -> compiled tasklet bundle (versioned tar) via CLI/CI
Tasklet executes under admin-runner and records per-step events to telemetry (trace_id, outcome, duration)
Automatic dry-run mode available and goroutine-safe: dry-run must not mutate production resources
RBAC enforced: tasks failing permission checks should not execute and must log audit event
Fallback policy: if a step's external dependency (e.g., Redis) is degraded, runtime routes to a safe-rollback step or halts with clear remediation hint
tasks: Spec: consolidate runbook authoring grammar (input YAML schema) - doc + examples
Compiler prototype: parse grammar -> IR -> tasklet serializer
Runtime adaptor: integrate tasklet executor into admin-runner with telemetry hooks
Safety: implement dry-run plumbing, permission checks, and step-level timeouts
CI: add compile step to runbook PR CI and automatic semantic checks
E2E: build smoke test harness with simulated external failures
Docs: author quickstart and postmortem template for automated remediations
technical_notes: Tasklet format: JSON-LD-ish flat list of steps; each step has id, kind, args, timeout_ms, retry_policy, rollback_step_id
IR decisions: compile-time constant expansion, prompt templating is disallowed (security) — must be parameter-only to avoid leaked secrets
Telemetry model: emit events to 'ops.tasklet.execution' with fields: tasklet_id, version, step_id, status, duration_ms, actor, trace_id
Storage: compiled bundles stored in s3://redwood-runbook-artifacts/<tasklet-id>/<version>.tar.gz with signed metadata file
Execution model: single-runner single-thread per tasklet to preserve step ordering; parallelism only allowed for explicit 'parallel' composite steps
Fallbacks: runtime will evaluate health probes (cache miss rates, p95 latency) and consult policy config (circuit breaker thresholds) before executing risky steps
decisions: Use a conservative subset of actions for v1: http requests (with domain allowlist), k8s patch, DB read-only queries, internal admin API calls; no arbitrary shell execution by default
Compile-time validation preferred over runtime heuristics for safety; CI must reject runbooks that reference forbidden endpoints
Audit trail persisted for every execution; minimal retention 90 days in secure logs
RBAC ties to existing IAM groups and SSO identities; admin-runner should reject non-approved actors
